questions.prompt: When one Dockerfile layer's cache is invalidated, what happens to the instructions after it?

options.text: Nothing; only that one layer rebuilds
Every layer after it is rebuilt too
The build fails
The layers below are skipped entirely

questions.explanation: A cache miss cascades: once a layer changes, no layer below it can be reused, so all subsequent instructions run again.

questions.prompt: Why copy the dependency manifest and install dependencies before copying the rest of the source?

options.text: It is required syntax
Dependencies change less often, so that layer stays cached across code edits and installs are skipped
It makes the image larger on purpose
It disables the build cache

questions.explanation: Because a cache miss cascades, putting the rarely-changing dependency install above the frequently-changing source keeps the expensive install layer cached.

questions.prompt: Why combine apt-get install and the cleanup of package lists into a single RUN?

options.text: It is the only valid syntax
Each RUN is a layer, so cleaning up in the same RUN keeps the removed files out of the image
It runs faster at container start
It publishes the ports automatically

questions.explanation: Cleaning up in a later RUN cannot shrink the image, because the earlier layer already contains the files. Doing it in the same RUN keeps them out.

questions.prompt: The instruction that sets the fixed executable a container always runs is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: ENTRYPOINT fixes the program that runs; CMD supplies default arguments that are easy to override at docker run.

questions.prompt: Which are good Dockerfile practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pin base image tags instead of using latest
Ship a .dockerignore to keep the context small and safe
Place volatile steps (copying source) after stable ones (installing deps)
Copy all source first, then install dependencies

questions.explanation: Pin versions, use a .dockerignore, and order stable-before-volatile. Copying source before installing deps defeats the cache.

questions.prompt: Given ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "http.server"] and CMD ["8000"], what does `docker run img 9000` do?

options.text: Fails, because you cannot pass arguments
Runs python -m http.server 9000, overriding the CMD default while keeping the ENTRYPOINT
Ignores 9000 and serves on 8000
Replaces the whole command with 9000

questions.explanation: Arguments after the image override CMD but not ENTRYPOINT, so the server runs on 9000 while the fixed program stays python -m http.server.
